With respect to the parks, national monuments and national historic sites, we note that the encouragement of enjoyment by recreational users is a congressionally established goal which should be actively pursued wherever compatible with the steward-ship or environmental preservation functions of the NPS with respect to such lands.
B. Bureau of Sport Fisheries and Wildlife (BSFW) -
As pointed out in the Draft Statement, BSFW is responsible for the management of some 30 million acres of public land and is charged with the primary responsibility of the protection and perpetuation of wildlife resources. Historically, BSFW has followed a fairly restrictive use policy similar to that of the National Park Service described above. The Association is in agreement as to the applicability of the "prohibited except where specifically permitted" regulatory approach when applied to BSFW lands. However, it is again emphasized that the Secretary does have a responsibility for promoting recreational use of this land to the extent that such use will not adversely affect environmental values. Accordingly, BSFW should be encouraged to actively review its land areas with a view towards designation of ORRV areas and trails wherever possible under the aforesaid criterion.
